sub: Named after al-ḥashr, “the gathering” into exile, in ayah 2
theme: The exile of Banū an-Naḍīr proves that no fortress protects against Allah. The surah teaches fair sharing of wealth, exposes the hypocrites’ empty promises, and ends by calling believers to prepare for tomorrow and know Allah’s names.
story: Revealed in Madinah, reportedly in 4 AH, about Banū an-Naḍīr, a Jewish tribe near Madinah, so it was also called Sūrat Banī an-Naḍīr. They had a peace treaty with the Prophet ﷺ, but reportedly plotted to drop a rock on him while he sat beside one of their walls.

Warned by revelation, he left and gave them ten days to leave Madinah. The hypocrite ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy promised them two thousand men, so they refused. The Muslims besieged their forts, and the promised help never came.

After some days they agreed to leave, taking what their camels could carry except weapons, and went to Khaybar and Syria. The surah draws the lessons: who receives the wealth left behind, what hypocrisy looks like, and who Allah is.

sections.title: Everything glorifies Allah; Banū an-Naḍīr’s forts fail and they are exiled
sections.meaning: Everything glorifies Allah. He drove Banū an-Naḍīr from their homes. No one expected them to leave, and they trusted their forts, but Allah reached them from where they never expected, filling their hearts with terror. Exile spared them worse in this world. Even cutting their palm trees was by Allah’s permission.
points: Everything in heaven and earth glorifies Allah, the Mighty, the Wise
He expelled them; their forts failed; take warning
Exile instead of worse; the Fire for those who oppose
Palms cut or left standing: both by Allah’s permission
sections.matters: It opens with a real event the listeners had just lived through. Walls, wealth and numbers failed a tribe that broke its treaty, not because of Muslim strength but because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. “Take warning, O people of vision” turns history into a lesson.
sections.story: Banū an-Naḍīr broke their treaty and reportedly plotted to kill the Prophet ﷺ. Given ten days to leave, they refused, trusting the hypocrites’ promise of help. After a short siege they left, taking what their camels could carry except weapons.
explained: Al-ḥashr is the gathering of Banū an-Naḍīr for exile, the first for them, with a later one under ʿUmar. Their forts were strong, and neither side expected a quick end. But Allah came at them from where they least expected: terror in their hearts. They pulled out doors and beams to carry off, and the believers broke down the rest.

Had Allah not written exile for them, they would have faced a harsher punishment in this world, and the Fire still awaits. That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. During the siege some palms were cut and burned, others left standing. When they called it corruption, Allah declared both choices were by His permission.
teaches: No wall or wealth protects against Allah.
Allah’s help can come as fear in the enemy’s heart.
Breaking promises brings its own ruin.
Look at what happens around you and take the lesson.
sections.hook: The surah opens with sabbaḥa lillāh (1) and closes with yusabbiḥu lahu (24), both ending “the Mighty, the Wise.” It starts on page 545, the same page where Al-Mujādilah ends.

sections.title: Wealth won without battle goes to the needy, Emigrants, Helpers, later believers
sections.meaning: Wealth gained without battle is fayʾ. The Prophet ﷺ distributes it, including to relatives, orphans, the needy and travellers, so it doesn’t circulate only among the rich. Take what the Messenger gives and avoid what he forbids. It also belongs to the poor Emigrants, the generous Helpers, and the believers who come after.
points: No horses or camels spent: this wealth is fayʾ
Shared out so wealth doesn’t stay among the rich
The poor Emigrants, driven from home: the truthful
The Helpers: loving, unenvious, putting others first even in need
Later believers: forgive us and them; cleanse our hearts
sections.matters: It sets out how public wealth is shared, and gives a principle for all of life: take what the Prophet ﷺ gives, leave what he forbids. Then it describes three kinds of believers and invites everyone after the Companions into the third.
sections.story: The Muslims asked for Banū an-Naḍīr’s property to be divided like battle spoils. Allah said it was fayʾ, for the Prophet ﷺ to distribute. He gave it to the Emigrants and a few poor Helpers, and the Helpers gladly agreed.
explained: The Muslims hadn’t ridden into battle for this wealth; Allah handed it over. So it isn’t split among fighters. The Prophet ﷺ used it for his family’s yearly needs and the Muslims’ interests, and for relatives, orphans, the needy and stranded travellers, so it never becomes dūlah, passed around among the rich. Whatever he gives or forbids, accept it.

Then three groups. The Emigrants lost homes and wealth for Allah; they are the truthful. The Helpers welcomed them with love, felt no envy at what they received, and put them first even when poor. Whoever is saved from shuḥḥ, the soul’s greed, succeeds. Those who come after pray for them, and for hearts free of resentment.
teaches: Wealth should circulate, not stay with the rich.
Take what the Prophet ﷺ brought; avoid what he forbade.
Give to others even when you need it yourself.
Being saved from greed is real success.
Pray for earlier believers and keep your heart free of resentment.
sections.hook: Three groups, three openings: “for the poor emigrants” (8), “and those who were settled in the Home” (9), “and those who come after them” (10). The duʿāʾ in 10 starts and ends with “Our Lord.”

sections.title: Hypocrites promise Banū an-Naḍīr help, then desert them like Shayṭān
sections.meaning: The hypocrites promised Banū an-Naḍīr: if you are expelled, we’ll leave with you; if you are fought, we’ll help. Allah says they are lying, and would run anyway. They fear the believers more than Allah and look united but are divided. They are like Shayṭān, who urges disbelief, then disowns.
points: Hypocrites promise to leave with them and fight for them
They won’t leave, won’t help, and would turn and run
They fear you more than Allah; united outside, divided inside
Like those just before them, who tasted the result
Like Shayṭān: “Disbelieve,” then “I am free of you”
sections.matters: Allah foretold exactly what would happen, and it did: the hypocrites stayed home. The section exposes a pattern that repeats: people who push others into wrong, then abandon them. It also points to the cure: fear Allah, not people.
sections.story: ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy and others sent word to Banū an-Naḍīr: stand firm, we have two thousand men, and we will leave or fight with you. Trusting this, they refused to go. When the siege came, no hypocrite came to help.
explained: Allah testifies the hypocrites are liars. If Banū an-Naḍīr are expelled, they won’t follow; if attacked, they won’t help; and if they did, they’d turn and run. They fear the believers more than Allah, because they don’t understand. They fight only from fortified towns or behind walls. Together they look united, but their hearts are split.

They are like those shortly before them, either Banū Qaynuqāʿ, exiled earlier, or the Quraysh at Badr, who tasted the result of their deeds. And they are like Shayṭān: he tells a person, “Disbelieve,” and once he does, says, “I am free of you; I fear Allah.” Both end in the Fire forever.
teaches: Don’t trust those who push you toward wrong; they will abandon you.
Fearing people more than Allah comes from lack of understanding.
Unity without faith is only on the surface.
Shayṭān’s promises end with him disowning you.
sections.hook: Ayah 12 answers 11 point by point: “we will leave with you” → they won’t leave; “we will aid you” → they won’t aid. Then two “like the example of”: those before (15), Satan (16).

sections.title: Check deeds for tomorrow; the Quran would split a mountain; Allah’s names
sections.meaning: Believers: fear Allah and check what you’ve sent ahead for tomorrow. Don’t forget Allah, or He makes you forget yourselves. The people of the Fire and of Paradise are not equal. Had this Quran come down on a mountain, it would split in awe. Then Allah describes Himself with His beautiful names.
points: Fear Allah; look at what you’ve sent ahead for tomorrow
Don’t forget Allah; Fire and Paradise are not equal
A mountain would split in awe of this Quran
He is Allah: Knower, Merciful, King, Pure, Peace, Mighty
Creator, Maker, Shaper; the best names; all glorify Him
sections.matters: After history and hypocrisy, the surah turns to every believer: look at yourself. It moves from self-checking, to the power of the Quran, to Allah’s names, so fear and love are built on knowing Him. Its closing ayat are reportedly a recommended morning and evening recitation.
sections.story: No specific incident. Once, reportedly, very poor visitors came to Madinah; the Prophet ﷺ recited ayah 18 in a talk, and people rushed to give until there were two heaps of food and clothes.
explained: Ghad, tomorrow, is the Day of Judgement, as certain and near as tomorrow. So check what you have sent ahead, good or bad. Taqwā is commanded before and after that check. Those who forgot Allah were made to forget their own good and sent nothing ahead. The people of Paradise, not of the Fire, are the winners.

If a mountain could understand this Quran, it would be humbled and split apart from fear of Allah. So what about human hearts? Then Allah is described: no god but Him, Knower of the unseen and seen, the Merciful, the King, the Pure, the Giver of safety, the Watcher, the Mighty, the Creator who shapes every form.
teaches: Check yourself today before you are checked tomorrow.
Forgetting Allah means neglecting what is good for you.
Let the Quran soften your heart.
sections.hook: “He is Allah” opens ayat 22, 23 and 24; 22 and 23 both add “other than whom there is no deity.” Taqwā is commanded twice in ayah 18.

groups.text: Everything in the heavens and earth glorifies Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.
Allah expelled Banū an-Naḍīr; their forts failed and terror took their hearts. Take warning.
Exile spared them worse in this world; the Fire awaits those who oppose Allah.
Palms cut or left standing during the siege were both by Allah’s permission.
Wealth gained without battle is shared by the Prophet ﷺ among those in need, not only the rich.
It is for the poor Emigrants, driven from their homes for Allah: the truthful.
The Helpers love the Emigrants and put them first, even when in need.
Later believers pray for those before them and for hearts free of resentment.
Hypocrites promise Banū an-Naḍīr support; Allah says they lie and would run.
They fear people more than Allah, fight from behind walls, and their hearts are divided.
Like earlier losers and like Shayṭān, who urges disbelief then disowns; both end in the Fire.
Fear Allah, check what you sent ahead, and don’t forget Him; Paradise’s people win.
A mountain would split in awe if this Quran came down on it.
He is Allah: no god but Him, Knower, Merciful, King, Creator, with the best names.

1.explain: Sabbaḥa: everything in the heavens and earth declares Allah free of every flaw, each in its own way. Al-ʿAzīz: never overpowered. Al-Ḥakīm: wise in all He decrees and commands.

2.explain: Allah expelled Banū an-Naḍīr li-awwali al-ḥashr, at the first gathering into exile. Their forts seemed unbeatable, but He cast terror into their hearts. They tore down their own houses to carry parts away, and the believers broke the rest.
2.why: Reportedly Banū an-Naḍīr broke their treaty and plotted to drop a rock on the Prophet ﷺ while he sat by their wall. Warned, he gave them ten days to leave. Promised help, they refused, and after a siege they left.

3.explain: Allah had written al-jalāʾ, exile, for them. Otherwise He would have punished them in this world, with killing or captivity, and the Fire still awaits them in the Hereafter.

4.explain: Shāqqū: they set themselves against Allah and His Messenger and broke their word. Whoever opposes Allah will find Him severe in punishment.

5.explain: Līnah: a date palm, either a fine variety or any palm. Cutting some and leaving others during the siege was by Allah’s permission, and it disgraced the defiant, who couldn’t save their own trees.
5.why: Banū an-Naḍīr called out: “You forbid corruption, so why cut the palms?” Some Muslims had cut trees; others held back, as the trees would come to the Muslims. Worried it was a sin, they asked, and this ayah came.

6.explain: Fayʾ: wealth that “returns” without fighting. The Muslims spurred no horses or camels for it; Allah gave His Messenger power over them. So it was his to distribute, not the fighters’ to split.
6.why: The Muslims asked the Prophet ﷺ to divide Banū an-Naḍīr’s property among them like battle spoils, and this ayah came. He gave it to the Emigrants and to two or three poor Helpers.

7.explain: Fayʾ from any town is for Allah and the Messenger, his relatives, orphans, the needy and stranded travellers, so it isn’t dūlah, circulating only among the rich. What the Messenger gives, take; what he forbids, avoid.
7.why: Reportedly some leading Muslims asked the Prophet ﷺ to take his pick and a quarter, as chiefs did before Islam, and leave them the rest. This ayah came.

8.explain: It is also for the poor Muhājirūn, driven from their homes and wealth, seeking Allah’s bounty and pleasure and supporting His religion. Some tied stones to their stomachs from hunger. Aṣ-ṣādiqūn: true in word and deed.

9.explain: The Anṣār settled in Madinah and in faith before them. They love the Emigrants, feel no envy at what they received, and prefer them even in khaṣāṣah, need. Whoever is saved from shuḥḥ, greedy selfishness, succeeds.
9.why: An Anṣārī, reportedly Abū Ṭalḥah, took home a hungry guest of the Prophet ﷺ. Having only the children’s food, he put them to sleep, put out the lamp and pretended to eat. This ayah came. Other reports name others.

10.explain: Those who come after, until the Last Day, pray: forgive us and our brothers who came first in faith, and put no ghill, resentment, in our hearts toward believers. You are Kind and Merciful.

11.explain: Look at the hypocrites promising their “brothers” among the People of the Book: “If you are expelled, we’ll go with you; we’ll obey no one against you; if you are fought, we’ll help you.” Allah testifies they lie.
11.why: ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy and others sent word to Banū an-Naḍīr: don’t leave, we have two thousand men and allies coming. Trusting this, they told the Prophet ﷺ they would stay. No help came.

12.explain: It happened exactly so: they neither left with them nor fought for them. Even if they had come to help, they would have turned and run, and Banū an-Naḍīr would still be left without help.

13.explain: Rahbah: fear. The hypocrites fear you believers more than they fear Allah. That is because they don’t understand: they fear what they can see and forget Allah.

14.explain: They won’t face you together except from fortified towns or behind walls. Among themselves their hostility is fierce. They look united, but their hearts are shattā, scattered, because they don’t use reason.

15.explain: They are like those just before them, either Banū Qaynuqāʿ, exiled shortly before, or the Quraysh defeated at Badr. They tasted the result of their deeds, and a painful punishment awaits.

16.explain: The hypocrites are like Shayṭān: he tells a person, “Disbelieve.” Once he does, Shayṭān says, “I am free of you; I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds.” He abandons him when it matters.

17.explain: So both, the one who misleads and the one who follows, end in the Fire forever. That is the reward of the wrongdoers.

18.explain: Believers: fear Allah and let each soul look at mā qaddamat li-ghad, what it has sent ahead for tomorrow, the Day of Judgement. Then fear Allah again. He is fully aware of everything you do.

19.explain: Don’t be like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves: they neglected their own good and sent nothing ahead. They are al-fāsiqūn, who have left His obedience.

20.explain: The people of the Fire and the people of Paradise are never equal. The people of Paradise are al-fāʾizūn, the winners, saved from punishment.

21.explain: If this Quran came down on a mountain able to understand, you would see it humbled and splitting from fear of Allah. These examples are given so people reflect on their own hard hearts.

22.explain: He is Allah, no god but Him. ʿĀlim al-ghayb wa ash-shahādah: He knows the unseen and the seen. Ar-Raḥmān ar-Raḥīm: His mercy covers everything, in this life and the next.

23.explain: Al-Malik, the King; al-Quddūs, the Pure; as-Salām, free of all flaws; al-Muʾmin, giver of safety; al-Muhaymin, the Watcher; al-ʿAzīz; al-Jabbār, who compels and mends; al-Mutakabbir, the Supreme. Glory be to Him above all partners.

24.explain: Al-Khāliq measures out, al-Bāriʾ brings into being, al-Muṣawwir gives every creature its shape. To Him belong al-asmāʾ al-ḥusnā, the best names. Everything glorifies Him, and the surah ends as it began.
